White Stone
WHYT STOHN
noun phrase
From Revelation 2:17, the token given to the overcomer at Pergamos: "a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it." White (Greek leukos) signifies purity, acquittal, and victory.

📖 Biblical Definition

The white stone is the second part of the reward promised to the overcomer at Pergamos: "and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it" (Rev 2:17). In the ancient world a white stone served as a token of acquittal in a court (over against the black stone of condemnation), as a ticket of admission to a feast, and as a mark of welcome and favor. Each sense enriches the promise. To the overcomer Christ gives the verdict of acquittal, the admission to the marriage supper of the Lamb, and the personal token of His favor. Upon the stone is written "a new name" — known only to the one who receives it, a name expressing the intimate, particular love between the Lord and that soul, the new identity granted to those made new in Christ. As the Lord said to Israel, "thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name" (Isa 62:2). The white stone thus gathers up acquittal, welcome, and a love so personal that its name is a secret between the Savior and the saved. It is the pledge that the believer who overcomes the world's pressure to compromise is fully pardoned, fully welcomed, and fully and uniquely known by his Lord.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The token given to the Pergamos overcomer in Revelation 2:17, bearing a new name known only to its receiver; in the ancient world a sign of acquittal, admission, and favor — here Christ's pledge of pardon, welcome, and a uniquely personal love.

📖 Key Scripture

Rev 2:17 — "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it."

Isa 62:2 — "And the Gentiles shall see thy righteousness, and all kings thy glory: and thou shalt be called by a new name, which the mouth of the LORD shall name."

Isa 65:15 — "And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen: for the Lord GOD shall slay thee, and call his servants by another name:"

Rev 3:12 — "Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The white stone is corrupted when its "new name" is taken for a charm of secret esoteric knowledge or self-invented identity, rather than the God-given name of pardon, welcome, and personal love granted in Christ.

expand to see more

Esoteric-charm misreading. Some treat the secret name as occult or gnostic knowledge, a hidden password earned by the initiated. The text says the opposite: the name is given by Christ to the one who overcomes by His grace, a token of acquittal and welcome, not a reward for esoteric attainment. The dictionary holds that the new name is the fruit of free pardon and personal love, written by the Lord, not decoded by the adept.

Self-made-identity misreading. A culture that prizes self-defined identity hears "new name" as a license to invent oneself. But in Scripture the new name is named by the mouth of the LORD (Isa 62:2); it is God's naming of the soul He has redeemed, expressing who the believer truly is in Christ. The dictionary recovers the order: identity is received from the Creator and Redeemer, not constructed by the creature. The white stone is Christ's word over us, sweeter and surer than any name we could give ourselves.
